desc: The Ministry of Defence is the department that ran the British side of the question from the 1950s to 2009 and that released, under compulsion, the two most substantial British artefacts: the Project Condign report in May 2006 and roughly sixty thousand pages of UFO desk files through The National Archives between May 2008 and June 2013. Its public position throughout was that UAP reports were of no defence significance. Its internal position, as recorded in its own released documents, was that a 1996 policy review commissioned a classified Defence Intelligence Staff study whose second stated objective was 'to identify any potential military technologies of interest'; that the study's chapter on potential related military technology and its paragraph on related military applications were withheld under the defence exemption; and that its chapter on other countries recorded the flat statement that there was 'no intelligence exchange or access or collaboration of any sort' with the United States and Canada on the topic - followed by four redacted lines. The Ministry's Directorate of Air Staff is recorded as the author organisation of the Condign report; its Air Secretariat and Secretariat (Air Staff) held the desk.
